quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you bring me the bill, please?
quests.hint: Both words fit the phrase, so ignore the meaning and use the vowel. Tight jaw or half-open?
quests.explanation: The word was "bill": a short vowel with the jaw nearly closed. "Bell" would open slightly wider and sound clearer.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪ/ is short and high-ish with the jaw nearly closed; /e/ is also short but the jaw opens further and the tongue lowers toward the middle.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɪ/ keep the jaw almost shut with relaxed lips. For /e/ lower the jaw slightly so a fingertip could fit between the teeth.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: I was looking at the lock.
quests.hint: Both words could work here. Listen to how the word begins: contact or curl?
quests.explanation: You caught "lock" - the tongue tip tapped the ridge behind the upper teeth before the vowel. "Rock" has no contact, only a curled tongue.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Contact versus no contact: /l/ touches the ridge; /r/ hovers below it.
quests.mouthPosition: If your tongue touches the roof, you are making /l/; if it doesn't, /r/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The frame fits both nouns. Focus on the first sound only.
quests.explanation: That was "wine": the lips rounded and glided with no touch of the teeth. "Vine" buzzes with the lip under the upper teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for a smooth glide (/w/) versus a buzzing fricative (/v/).
quests.mouthPosition: Check in a mirror: teeth visible on the lip for /v/, lips rounded for /w/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same start and end, and both make sense here. How long is the vowel?
quests.explanation: "Heel" holds a tense, high vowel a little longer before the /l/. "Hill" is quick and relaxed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Two things separate these vowels: duration and tongue tension. /iː/ is held longer and sounds bright and tight; /ɪ/ is clipped and sounds softer, almost muffled by comparison.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the jaw nearly closed for both, but make /iː/ tighter: lips spread, tongue pushed high and forward. /ɪ/ needs no effort at all - let everything go slack.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Focus on the very start of the word, ignoring the rest of the phrase. Hiss or pop?
quests.explanation: In this phrase, "fork" started with a breathy hiss from the lip and teeth. "Pork" starts with a lip pop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A stop blocks the airflow completely and releases it with a burst; a fricative squeezes the air through a narrow gap and keeps it flowing. Listen for a burst versus a hiss.
quests.mouthPosition: For the stop, close the articulators fully and release. For the fricative, leave a narrow gap and let air rustle through.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The phrase fits either word. Listen to the friction at the start: soft or sharp?
quests.explanation: You heard "thick": a soft, airy sound with the tongue against the teeth. "Sick" starts with a sharper hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /θ/ sounds soft and diffuse; /s/ sounds sharp and high-pitched.
quests.mouthPosition: Look in a mirror: you should see the tongue tip for /θ/ but not for /s/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Steady rounded vowel or one that glides?
quests.explanation: "Code" starts relaxed and rounds as it goes. "Cord" is steady and rounded from the beginning.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are long enough to notice. Ask yourself whether the vowel holds the same shape throughout (/ɔː/) or changes shape (/əʊ/).
quests.mouthPosition: Say /ɔː/ with a tall, round mouth held still; say /əʊ/ starting relaxed and closing the lips.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: She was standing next to the cart.
quests.hint: Both words work in the phrase. Is the vowel long and deep, or short and bright?
quests.explanation: The word was "cart": a long, open vowel from the back of the mouth. "Cat" has a short, bright, forward vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɑː/ is held longer and sounds deeper; /æ/ is quick and bright.
quests.mouthPosition: Say /ɑː/ as if the dentist asked you to open wide; /æ/ is the same openness but with a sideways smile and a shorter beat.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both fit. Are the lips neutral or rounded in the vowel?
quests.explanation: "Cup" kept the lips neutral and the vowel flat, and it ended with the lips closing. "Cop" rounds them slightly and sounds deeper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short, so rely on lip shape: rounded for /ɒ/, unrounded for /ʌ/.
quests.mouthPosition: Notice your lips: a small circle for /ɒ/, a neutral shape for /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the end of the word. Is the vowel stretched and the ending buzzy?
quests.explanation: It was "peas": a long vowel and a buzz at the end. "Peace" would end in a crisp hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, /z/ lengthens the vowel before it and has a soft buzz; /s/ shortens the vowel and ends with a crisp hiss. In final position the buzz can be weak, so vowel length is the most reliable cue.
quests.mouthPosition: Hold the tongue behind the upper teeth. For /s/ end with a sharp hiss after a short vowel; for /z/ stretch the vowel and finish with a softer buzz.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both are verbs. Does the tongue tip touch the ridge behind the teeth at the start, or curl back?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "read": the tongue curled back at the start. "Lead" touches the ridge behind the upper teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /l/ sounds clear and light; /r/ sounds darker and slightly rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the tongue tip: contact for /l/, hover for /r/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The phrase suits both. Voiced or voiceless at the start?
quests.explanation: "Chin" starts with a breathy, voiceless /tʃ/. "Gin" starts with a buzzing /dʒ/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Voicing is the only change; listen for the buzz in /dʒ/.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the throat to feel the vibration.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the vowel in the middle of the word.
quests.explanation: That was "left": a half-open vowel with a clear, crisp sound. "Lift" is tighter and more closed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The vowels are close, so listen for jaw opening: /ɪ/ feels tight and closed, /e/ feels a little more open.
quests.mouthPosition: Say /ɪ/ with hardly any jaw movement, then drop the jaw a little for /e/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: I found a sheet by the door.
quests.hint: The sentence suits either noun. Focus on the hush or hiss at the start.
quests.explanation: "Sheet" begins with a broad hush and rounded lips. "Seat" begins with a sharp, thin hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Compare the pitch of the friction: /ʃ/ is a deeper 'shh', /s/ is a bright 'sss'.
quests.mouthPosition: Say 'shh' as if asking for quiet, then smile and say 'sss'.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: We thought about it all night.
quests.hint: Both words are grammatical here. Where does the friction come from at the start?
quests.explanation: The word was "thought": the friction came from the tongue between the teeth. "Fought" comes from the lower lip against the upper teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The two sounds are very similar in loudness, so listen to the softer, more diffuse quality of /θ/ against the crisper hiss of /f/.
quests.mouthPosition: Look in a mirror: the tongue tip is visible for /θ/, the lip moves for /f/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: The clue was hidden under the sofa.
quests.hint: Listen for a puff of breath at the start.
quests.explanation: "Clue" opens with a breathy /k/ before the tongue moves to /l/. "Glue" opens softly with voice from the start.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /k/ is released with a burst of breath before the vowel; /ɡ/ moves directly into the vowel.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the release gentle for /ɡ/ and let the voice start at once.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Lips or tongue? Focus on the opening sound.
quests.explanation: You heard "rake": the tongue tip curled back and the lips stayed fairly still. "Wake" starts with rounded lips.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /w/ is a lip glide: the lips round and open while the back of the tongue rises; /r/ is a tongue glide: the tip curls back with only slight lip rounding.
quests.mouthPosition: For /w/ push the lips into a tight round then open quickly into the vowel. For /r/ curl the tongue tip back and keep the lips relaxed.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both fit. Listen to the vowel length and the ending.
quests.explanation: "Price" has a slightly shorter vowel and a crisp hiss at the end. "Prize" stretches the vowel and ends with a buzz.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A longer vowel signals /z/; a shorter vowel and a strong hiss signal /s/.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel your throat vibrate through the end of /z/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The ending is the only difference. Tongue tip or back of the tongue?
quests.explanation: In this phrase you heard "mud": the tongue tip closed against the ridge. "Mug" closes at the back of the tongue, and the sound is duller.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Front versus back closure, same voicing.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel where the tongue touches: front or back.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The phrase works either way. Does the tongue tip touch to start?
quests.explanation: "Lane" begins with contact at the ridge behind the teeth. "Rain" begins with a curled tongue and no contact.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /l/ is made with the tongue tip touching the ridge behind the upper teeth, letting air flow around the sides; British /r/ is made with the tongue tip curled slightly back and not touching anything, often with lips a little rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: For /l/ press the tongue tip firmly against the ridge behind the upper teeth. For /r/ curl the tongue tip back and keep it away from the roof of the mouth, lips slightly rounded.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both make sense here. Front of the tongue or back?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "gate": the closure was at the back of the tongue, so the start sounds duller. "Date" would release with the tongue tip at the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for a brighter click (alveolar) versus a duller pop (velar).
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip down for the velar stop.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Compare the vowels: dull and short, or bright and wide?
quests.explanation: "Hut" is short, dull and central. "Hat" opens the jaw wide and sounds brighter.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue is forward and low for /æ/, but sits in the centre of the mouth for /ʌ/. To the ear, /æ/ sounds brighter and /ʌ/ sounds duller and flatter.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the front of your tongue rise toward your teeth for /æ/; for /ʌ/ the tongue stays lazy and flat.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the consonant after the /f/. Contact or curl?
quests.explanation: That was "flight": after the /f/, the tongue tip touched the ridge. In "fright" it would curl back.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In a consonant cluster the /l/ or /r/ follows another consonant, so the difference is smaller. /l/ needs tongue contact at the ridge; /r/ needs a curled tongue tip and often shortens or devoices the first consonant slightly.
quests.mouthPosition: Say the first consonant, then for /l/ touch the tongue tip to the ridge, for /r/ curl it back without touching.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both make sense. Listen to the vowel length and the ending.
quests.explanation: "Kid" holds the vowel a little longer and closes softly. "Kit" is shorter and finishes with a crisp stop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Ignore the final release; listen to how long the vowel is.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the throat relaxed for /d/; tighten and stop for /t/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Focus on the beginning of the word. Breath, or straight into the vowel?
quests.explanation: "Heat" opens with a puff of breath before the vowel. "Eat" starts the vowel directly.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /h/ is a breathy sound made in the throat, with the mouth already in the position of the following vowel; the alternative is a word that starts directly with the vowel. The cue is breath at the start.
quests.mouthPosition: Open the mouth in the vowel position and push out a gentle breath before voicing.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is there a small puff of breath at the start of the word, or does the vowel begin directly?
quests.explanation: The word was "air": it began with the vowel, no breath first. "Hair" begins with a soft puff.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for a puff of breath before the vowel.
quests.mouthPosition: Hold your palm in front of your mouth: you feel warm air for /h/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both fit. Listen for a small breath before the vowel.
quests.explanation: "Harm" begins with a puff of breath. "Arm" starts straight in with the open vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A word with /h/ begins with a soft rush of air.
quests.mouthPosition: Do not close the lips or tongue for /h/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to how the vowel begins: high and tight, or more open?
quests.explanation: Here, "bear" began more open, with the jaw about half down. "Beer" starts high and tight.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In careful British English, /ɪə/ begins with a high front vowel and glides to a schwa, while /eə/ begins lower and more open. The start of the vowel tells them apart. (Some speakers flatten /eə/ into a single long vowel, but it stays lower than /ɪə/.)
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɪə/ begin with the tongue high and the jaw nearly shut. For /eə/ begin with the jaw a little more open, then relax into schwa in both.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same start, same end. Is the vowel round and open, or tight and thin?
quests.explanation: It was "chop", with rounded lips and a deep, open vowel. "Chip" is thinner and higher.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Bright and thin (/ɪ/) versus deep and round (/ɒ/) is the simplest way to hear the difference.
quests.mouthPosition: Go from a tight, slightly smiling mouth (/ɪ/) to an open, rounded mouth (/ɒ/).

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Focus on the ending: does anything follow the /l/?
quests.explanation: "Milk" ends with the /l/ followed by a quick /k/ from the back of the tongue. "Mill" ends on the /l/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The cluster differs at the end only: /nd/ vs /nt/, /ld/ vs /lt/. Listen for how long the nasal or lateral lasts.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch your throat: buzz continues for the voiced cluster.
